brief_points: Miriam has metastatic breast cancer with two biologies at once: breast and neuroendocrine. Current protocols only account for the first, so standard treatment falls short.

The aim is to reach no evidence of disease with a therapy designed from her own tumor. Today the main route is a personalized vaccine. Other immunotherapies are also made from her own cells, such as TIL or CAR-T, and her doctors will weigh which one has the most evidence for her case.
The campaign pays for the tests that read the tumor in depth, for second opinions, and for getting to the trial or lab that can make that therapy, wherever it is.
There are ways to help beyond money: clinical review, outreach, tech, or just showing up.

twofaces.title: One tumor, two faces
twofaces.intro: It is not one tumor: it is two biologies in the same body, and both must be treated at once.
twofaces.ne_sub: the one we need to know
twofaces.close2: Treating only one selects for the other.
twofaces.sr: Tumor schematic. Luminal breast, the known part: hormone receptors, HER2 negative, amplification of FGFR1 (8p11) and of the 11q13 cluster (CCND1, FGF3/4/19), and an ESR1 mutation in ctDNA. In the liver metastasis (2026) the estrogen receptor is now negative. Neuroendocrine differentiation (Cg/Syn in 80% of the neoplastic cells in 2024; focal and heterogeneous in 2026), barely known: RB1 variants seen in blood and not confirmed in tissue, and somatostatin receptors (SSTR), the PRRT target. Block one side and it escapes through the other; it must be treated as a whole.
twofaces.legend_rec: Receptors: targets to attack (HR and SSTR).
twofaces.legend_amp: Amplifications: extra copies that push the tumor.
twofaces.legend_mut: Mutations: resistances the tumor builds to keep growing.
twofaces.legend_rb1: RB1: a brake altered in blood, not confirmed in tissue.
twofaces.legend_her2: HER2: a receptor she does not have (no target).

entry_disclaimer.title: New molecular and imaging findings
entry_disclaimer.body: Liquid biopsies (April–May 2026) have revealed new alterations: ESR1 D538G (endocrine resistance) and RB1 mutations (a predictor of neuroendocrine transformation). The Ga-68 DOTATOC PET-CT confirms multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor (SSTR) overexpression — a new therapeutic target via radioligand therapy (PRRT). The molecular profile has become more complex and reinforces the need to explore the neuroendocrine pathway in parallel with the breast (luminal) one.

home.s3_heading: What current protocols don't cover, we cover.
home.s3_subheading: Current protocols only account for half of the tumor's biology: they're built for standard HR+ breast cancer, and Miriam's is not.
home.s3_p1: Histologically it is a luminal breast carcinoma (HR+/HER2−). But IHC detected neuroendocrine differentiation. That second biology is not part of the current standard protocol.
home.s3_p2: Practical result: hormonal treatment covers the breast (luminal) component. The neuroendocrine component, with its own dynamics and targets, is left unaddressed.
home.s3_p3: The oncology team cannot prescribe off-protocol without solid evidence. Generating that evidence requires advanced panels and international review boards: the molecular rebiopsy and the international molecular tumor board (WIN) were done in 2026, and now the tissue needs analyzing and the tumor needs tracking. None of this is funded by public healthcare for a low-frequency case.
home.s3_pet_paragraph: Gallium PET: multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor overexpression (SSTR) and focal uptake in the right breast tail. The tumor expresses a target that breast protocols do not contemplate as standard, opening the radioligand path (PRRT).

llano.q1_a: A breast cancer that spread to the bones and, since July 2026, to the liver. It's mostly luminal, the type that usually depends on hormones, but some of its cells have features of another type, called neuroendocrine.
llano.q2_a: Guidelines treat it as a luminal breast cancer and leave the neuroendocrine part out. Hormone therapies stopped holding it back. And in the liver, the test for the estrogen receptor, the very target of those therapies, came back negative.
llano.q3_q: Is there a way to target it?
llano.q3_a: Yes, there are leads. Analysis of the tumor, including cell by cell, has found possible weak points: altered or active genes that some treatments use as targets. They're still hypotheses, and need confirming first.
llano.q4_a: Since {desde} she's been on Dato-DXd, an antibody that carries a drug to the tumor, in the TROPION-Breast06 trial. And at Dana-Farber, her liver and bone biopsies are being read cell by cell. The first results are in.
llano.q4_a_sin_linea: At Dana-Farber, her liver and bone biopsies are being read cell by cell, to look for the targets of a therapy made for her. The first results are in.

ruta.title: From tissue to a therapy made for her tumour
ruta.intro: The vaccine trials explored in June were not accessible then (there was not enough tissue to manufacture one); they are not closed for good and are still being reviewed. This is the route to build a therapy from her own tumor: five steps, each depending on the one before. Today the case is at step {paso}, and treatment to control the disease continues in parallel.

tejido.texto: There is tumour tissue from several biopsies (the latest from this summer), stored so it can be analysed in depth.

leer.texto: Sequence the tumour’s DNA, see which genes each cell expresses and compare it with her healthy blood, keeping only what belongs to the tumour. Breast, bone and liver tissue is already at the Dana-Farber lab (the last shipment arrived on 23 September). The healthy blood sample is still pending.

dianas.texto: Look for the mutations only the tumour has and that her immune system could recognise. That also requires knowing her HLA: the molecules that show pieces of the tumour to her T cells and decide which ones can be recognised. Her HLA has not been typed yet.

disenar.texto: Those targets can be used to make a personalised vaccine or to prepare T cells that recognise them (TCR-T, TIL). Another path, CAR-T, targets proteins on the tumour surface and is chosen from other data. More than one can be combined, and the aim is the one with the most evidence for her case. The decision belongs to her medical team.

llegar.texto: A clinical trial or a manufacturer able to make it. The search is open to any country.

ruta.nota: Explanatory material: it describes the path, it does not promise results. Decisions are made by her medical team.

ciencia.simple_body: No jargon: what's happening to Miriam, why her case is different, and what's needed now.
ciencia.simple_a1: A breast cancer that has spread to the bones and, since this summer, to the liver. What is unusual is that it behaves like two diseases at once: partly like a “hormonal” breast cancer and largely like a different type (neuroendocrine). Two faces of the same tumour.
ciencia.simple_a2: The protocols treat it as an ordinary breast cancer and attack only one of its two faces. The other goes untreated, and the tumour finds a way to keep advancing. This summer’s liver biopsy fits that picture: there, the tumour no longer has the estrogen receptor, which is exactly what the hormone treatments targeted, and it keeps its neuroendocrine face.
ciencia.simple_q3: Is there a way to target it?
ciencia.simple_a3: Yes. Analysis of the tumor has found specific "weak points" that could be treated with targeted therapies. These are promising hypotheses, not a guaranteed cure: that's why they must be confirmed before acting.
ciencia.simple_a4: Two things at once. A new treatment within a clinical trial is expected to start in October, to hold the disease back. And her tumour samples are already in a Dana-Farber lab in Boston, where they are read cell by cell and gene by gene to look for the targets of a therapy made for her.
ciencia.simple_more: A medical or science professional and want the detail, with biomarkers and tables? Switch to "For professionals" above.
ciencia.ai_summary_text: Miriam González ({age}) has metastatic breast cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (BC-NED), HER2 0, FGFR1 and CCND1 amplification, and bone and liver metastases. The August 2026 liver biopsy (report of 21 September) showed ER 0%. She is in screening for a datopotamab deruxtecan (anti-TROP-2) trial, and her tissue is being analysed at Dana-Farber (single-cell RNA-seq and exome). Donate: gofund.me/3e25cae99

ciencia.axes_note_cierre: The Dana-Farber analysis and target immunohistochemistry on the liver (TROP-2, SSTR2, DLL3) could confirm or rule out these axes.
ciencia.goal_n_of_1_desc: A treatment designed for a single patient, built on her tumour’s actual profile rather than the HR+ average. Two things run in parallel today: a treatment to control the disease (a datopotamab deruxtecan trial, expected from October 2026) and an in-depth reading of the tumour, which is where the targets of a personalised therapy would come from.
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines: Why doesn't this tumor fit the protocols?
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines_text: On paper this is a {luminal} breast cancer (HR+/HER2−). In the 2024 diagnostic biopsy, 80% of the neoplastic cells expressed chromogranin and synaptophysin (CD56 negative); on review of the same block in 2026 the expression is focal and heterogeneous, and the markers also appear in bone (synaptophysin) and in the liver (chromogranin A and synaptophysin), with no percentage.
ciencia.thesis: The thesis: biology, not the organ of origin, should guide treatment.
ciencia.thesis_goal: Goal: a therapy designed on the profile of this tumor (N-of-1), decided by her medical team.
ciencia.updates_2026_subtitle: Results generated in 2026 that complement the 2024 primary-tissue profile.
ciencia.ctdna_what: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from peripheral blood analyzed by NGS. A standard blood draw detects mutations, amplifications and clonal dynamics without a tissue biopsy. Especially useful in bone-only disease, where tissue is scarce or molecularly uninformative.
ciencia.imaging_intro: The bone metastases reveal a target visible in vivo: they express {sstr}, the target of {prrt}. Standard breast-cancer protocols do not consider this route.
ciencia.imaging_what: PET with the 68Ga-DOTATOC radiotracer, which binds mainly the somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2). Visualizes in vivo which lesions express SSTR2 and could therefore respond to radioligand therapy (PRRT).
ciencia.article_fallback_notice: This article is not yet available in English. Showing the Spanish version.
ciencia.snapshot_intro: The essentials in ten seconds, before the molecular detail.
ciencia.snapshot_diagnosis: Invasive carcinoma (NST) with neuroendocrine differentiation (BC-NED) · HR+/HER2 0 · premenopausal · de novo stage IV, dx January 2024
ciencia.snapshot_drivers: FGFR1 (8p11) · CCND1 + FGF3/4/19 (11q13) · 13 and 20 copies in the 2024 primary
ciencia.snapshot_resistance: ESR1 D538G and 3 RB1 variants in ctDNA (Apr–May 2026), not confirmed in bone tissue · ER loss in the liver metastasis
ciencia.snapshot_target: TROP-2: target of the ADC (not measured in tissue) · SSTR+ on Ga-68 PET, bone only (May 2026)
ciencia.snapshot_status: ECOG 0 · bone and liver metastases · off the BG-75202 trial (KAT6i) since 9 Sep due to liver progression · in screening for TROPION-Breast06 (Dato-DXd)
ciencia.snapshot_grade: Primary 2024: ER 95% · PR 5% · HER2 0 · Ki67 60% · G2 · Liver 2026: ER 0% · PR 5% · HER2 0

ciencia.ctdna_dynamics_intro: The tumor isn’t static: ctDNA tracks its changes (VAF) across three plasma draws, with no biopsy needed.

ciencia.goal_lab_desc: Paloma Cejas, co-director of the Center for Functional Cancer Epigenetics at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, is collaborating on the molecular study. Her lab holds paraffin material from all three sites: breast (2024), bone (July 2026) and liver (August 2026). The plan is single-cell RNA-seq with 10x Genomics Flex, which works on paraffin, and exome sequencing.
ciencia.goal_lab_note: To separate what belongs to the tumour from what is inherited, her normal DNA (blood) is still needed; it has not yet been sent to Boston.

ciencia.ficha_tejido: All the tissue and its status
ciencia.why_no_fit_protocols_text: The tumor also carries amplification of {fgfr1} and {ccnd1}. Current protocols recommend treating it as standard luminal and ignoring the {neuroendocrino} component.
ciencia.why_no_fit_oms_text: The 2019 WHO classification reserves “neuroendocrine neoplasm of the breast” for tumors with more than 90% neuroendocrine cells; this is a carcinoma NST with neuroendocrine differentiation, which falls outside that category and is treated with the luminal breast-cancer guidelines. The evidence on its prognosis is retrospective and inconsistent across series; no published cohort is de novo stage IV in premenopausal patients. On this site we call it {bcned} as a working label, not as a diagnostic category.
ciencia.estado_cuarta_linea: In fourth line since {fecha}: datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks in TROPION-Breast06 (Vall d'Hebron); the clinical course documents her inclusion and schedules the first cycle that day.

ciencia.panel_nota: Consultation support material: it describes which analyses exist and what each one answers; it is not a treatment indication. What is analysed and how is decided by the lab doing it, and clinical decisions by the treating medical team.
ciencia.patologia_limites_titulo: What these reads do not say
ciencia.nota_copias_titulo: How to read the FGFR1 and CCND1 copy numbers
ciencia.nota_copias: FGFR1: 13 copies in the 2024 primary (TSO500; the sender estimated 75% tumor and the laboratory warns that the copy number is not reliable below 50%; VIGex measured 50% in the same block). In the 2026 bone, the clinical FoundationOne CDx report says “FGFR1 amplification” with no figure; the 33 copies of FGFR1 and 37 of the 11q13 cluster come from the research file of that analysis (“for research use only”, computational purity 61%). Different platforms, samples and purities: the amplification is firm, the figures are not comparable with each other.

team.title: The team
team.subtitle: An engineer, an international team and artificial intelligence, searching for the therapy that standard oncology doesn't yet consider.
team.network_origin_body: A scientific and technological research association (biotech, AI, data). We're getting it ready. In the meantime, you can help the case:
notus_list: We do not promise cures. We document biological hypotheses and their real probabilities.
We do not use “fight” or “warrior” language. We talk biology, data and clinical decisions.
We do not replace the medical team. We add external analysis; clinical decisions are signed by Miriam's oncology team.
We do not publish clinical data without review. Transparency demands rigor, not speed.
We're not a perfect AI. The AI we use sometimes hallucinates — and the humans reviewing it do too. If you spot a typo, let us know.
team.how_it_formed: A team that formed on its own: medicine, science, AI and technology, each contributing from their own field, with a single goal: to let the tumor's biology guide the treatment. Clinical decisions always remain with Miriam's medical team.

historia.fallback_notice: This chapter is not yet available in English. Showing the Spanish version.
historia.pending_notice: This is the most personal part of the site, and it's being written by someone who knows Miriam closely: who she is beyond cancer, what she did, and why she does what she does. It'll be ready very soon. Meanwhile, you can follow the day-to-day on her social channels or get to know the case in The science.
historia.story_teaser_1: Three years ago, Miriam was working full-time as a software developer and creating content about technology. Within a matter of months, her life took a radical turn.
historia.story_teaser_2: It all began with back pain, physiotherapy sessions and GPs who couldn't find a solution. As the pain persisted and she wasn't getting answers, she decided to arrange an MRI scan herself. One Thursday in January 2024, she found the test results in her inbox: “probable vertebral metastases”. A couple of weeks later, the definitive diagnosis arrived: “Stage IV breast cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation”.
historia.story_teaser_3: For two years, Miriam has been rebuilding her life piece by piece with treatments that have given her time and peace of mind, but with an end date. In 2026, everything has moved forward at breakneck speed. What if these advances, combined with the specific nature of her cancer, opened doors that previously seemed closed?
historia.story_teaser_4: In this story, we want to tell you about Miriam's case, her journey and her daily routine so that you can truly understand what it means to live with stage 4 cancer.

esquemaTumor.titulo: A breast tumor with neuroendocrine features
esquemaTumor.lede: It is a breast-type (luminal) tumor. Some of its cells also carry neuroendocrine features. In the two biopsies read cell by cell (liver and bone, 2026) those cells are mixed within the tumor, not a separate camp. What changes with the tissue and the technique (staining, DNA, RNA, PET) is how it looks.
esquemaTumor.clave_er: Estrogen receptor: present in the breast. In the liver, staining came back 0%, yet its gene is still switched on in the RNA.
esquemaTumor.clave_her2: HER2: she does not have it (0 in four readings).
esquemaTumor.clave_copias: Extra copies of the FGFR1 and CCND1 genes.
esquemaTumor.clave_sangre: Changes in RB1 and ESR1: only in blood, at a very low fraction (under 2%), and in no tissue.
esquemaTumor.alt_tumor: Diagram of a luminal tumor with neuroendocrine-feature dots scattered throughout it, without forming a separate group.
esquemaTumor.alt_celula: Diagram of a tumor cell. Inside the nucleus, an estrogen receptor and two marks for extra DNA copies (FGFR1 and CCND1). On the membrane, a crossed-out HER2 receptor, because she does not have it.
esquemaTumor.alt_sangre: Diagram of a drop of blood with many normal DNA fragments and two altered ones, those of RB1 and ESR1.
esquemaTumor.nota: Neither the cell, nor the number of dots, nor their position is data.
esquemaTumor.nota_procedencia: What comes from the cell-by-cell reading (scattered neuroendocrine features, estrogen receptor in the RNA) is first results. The rest comes from reports from 2024 to 2026.
esquemaTumor.cifras_titulo: The figures, one by one, with their source
esquemaTumor.cifras_lead: The full tables, report by report:
cifras: Estrogen receptor (ER): present in the breast, absent on liver staining · 95%, 100% and 85% in three readings of the breast tumor (2024-2026) · 0% in the liver (2026)

…yet the estrogen receptor gene is still switched on in the RNA of the 2026 biopsies read cell by cell, although liver staining came back 0%. (It was also high in the RNA of the 2024 breast tumor, where staining was positive.)
Progesterone receptor (PR): discordant between laboratories in the breast (5%, 100%, 20%) · 5% in the liver (2026)
HER2: she does not have it (0) in four readings: three of the breast tumor and one of the liver
Somatostatin receptors: the DOTATOC PET (May 2026) saw them in several bone lesions, not all, and the liver had no lesions yet · the SSTR2 gene barely shows in the cell-by-cell RNA (2026)

Extra copies of the FGFR1 gene · 13 copies (breast 2024, TSO500) · amplified in bone 2026 (FoundationOne; 33 copies in its research annex) · 5-7 copies in blood 2026 (diluted signal) · active in liver and bone RNA
Extra copies of CCND1 and its neighbours FGF3/FGF4/FGF19 · 20 and 18 copies (breast 2024) · 37 in the 2026 bone research annex · 6-7.6 in blood
A single point change in the estrogen receptor gene (ESR1 D538G), only in blood and at a very low fraction · 0.24% (April) · 0.84-1.38% (May) · not seen in the April Guardant nor in any tissue
RB1 alterations, a cell-cycle brake, seen only in blood and at a very low fraction · three in April (1.58%, 1.48%, 0.28%) · only one in May (0.19-0.68%) · none in tissue (breast 2024, bone 2026)
Few mutations overall (3-4 per megabase) · microsatellites stable or with low instability
PIK3CA not mutated in breast 2024, bone 2026 and blood 2026 (one of the most frequent alterations in this tumor type, and she does not have it)

Neuroendocrine features (chromogranin, synaptophysin, INSM1) · 80% of tumor cells in one reading of the 2024 breast biopsy; another 2024 reading did not report them · 2026 re-read: focal chromogranin, heterogeneous synaptophysin, mosaic INSM1 · bone 2026: synaptophysin positive (little tumor tissue; chromogranin not reported) · liver 2026: chromogranin A and synaptophysin positive, no percentage · cell by cell: scattered, no separate group; real INSM1 in the liver
Liver and bone: compatible with the same tumor (same main genes, FGFR1 active in both, RNA copy profile compatible with a single clone; the exome could confirm it)
Almost no defences inside: a "cold" tumor · T lymphocytes around 1 in 100 cells in the liver, or fewer · TILs <5% in the breast tumor (2026) · PD-L1 CPS 0 in breast (2024) and liver (2026)
Division rate (Ki67) · 60% breast 2024 · 40% 2026 re-read · ≈15% bone 2026 (small, decalcified sample) · not reported in the liver. Not a trend: different tissues and methods
esquemaTumor.limites_titulo: What this diagram does not say
esquemaTumor.limite_2: Cell-by-cell results (status as of {fecha}): figures from the analysis by Polaris, Miriam's system, on the lab's data, not from the lab report; two small pieces of two lesions.
esquemaTumor.limite_3: Bone is decalcified to be cut and that damages RNA: its reading is noisier.
esquemaTumor.limite_4: RNA is not protein: what is "switched on" must be confirmed by tissue staining.
esquemaTumor.limite_5: The exome (WES) and HLA type are missing: without them there are no tumor-specific mutations nor candidates for a personalised therapy.
esquemaTumor.limite_6: Copy figures come from different tests and samples (2024 breast, 2026 bone, blood) and are not comparable; blood figures are fractions under 2%.
esquemaTumor.limite_7: The PET detects somatostatin receptors as a whole, without telling subtypes apart; RNA measures one specific gene (SSTR2).
esquemaTumor.limite_8: The discordance between 0% ER staining in the liver and an active ER program in RNA is open and in front of her medical team. Nothing on this page recommends treatment.
